Let

\[ S = \sum_{k=0}^{2026} k \binom{2k}{k} 2^k. \]

Compute the remainder when \( S \) is divided by 2027. (Note that 2027 is prime.)

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let

\[
p=2027,\qquad a_k=\binom{2k}{k}2^k.
\]

All congruences below are modulo \(p\).

### 1. Relate \(S\) to the unweighted sum

We have

\[
\frac{a_{k+1}}{a_k}
=
\frac{\binom{2k+2}{k+1}}{\binom{2k}{k}}\cdot 2
=
\frac{2(2k+1)}{k+1}\cdot 2
=
\frac{4(2k+1)}{k+1}.
\]

Thus

\[
(k+1)a_{k+1}=4(2k+1)a_k=(8k+4)a_k,
\]

so

\[
8ka_k=(k+1)a_{k+1}-4a_k.
\]

Let

\[
B=\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}a_k.
\]

Then

\[
8S=\sum_{k=1}^{p-1}8ka_k
=\sum_{k=1}^{p-1}\bigl((k+1)a_{k+1}-4a_k\bigr).
\]

Now

\[
\sum_{k=1}^{p-1}(k+1)a_{k+1}
=\sum_{j=2}^{p}ja_j
\equiv S-a_1
= S-4,
\]

because \(pa_p\equiv 0\pmod p\). Also

\[
\sum_{k=1}^{p-1}a_k=B-1.
\]

Therefore

\[
8S\equiv (S-4)-4(B-1)=S-4B,
\]

so

\[
7S\equiv -4B \pmod p. \tag{1}
\]

It remains to compute \(B\).

---

### 2. Compute \(B\)

Use the constant-term notation \([t^0]\). Since

\[
t+2+t^{-1}=t^{-1}(1+t)^2,
\]

we have

\[
[t^0](t+2+t^{-1})^k=\binom{2k}{k}.
\]

Set

\[
q(t)=2(t+2+t^{-1}).
\]

Then

\[
a_k=[t^0]q(t)^k,
\]

and hence

\[
B=\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}[t^0]q^k
=[t^0]\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}q^k
=[t^0]\frac{1-q^p}{1-q}.
\]

In \(\mathbb{F}_p\),

\[
q(t)=2t+4+2t^{-1},
\]

so by Frobenius,

\[
q(t)^p=2t^p+4+2t^{-p}.
\]

Thus

\[
\frac{1-q^p}{1-q}
=
\frac{-3-2t^p-2t^{-p}}{-3-2t-2t^{-1}}
=
\frac{2t^{p+1}+3t+2t^{1-p}}{2t^2+3t+2}.
\]

Let

\[
D(t)=2t^2+3t+2.
\]

Let \(\alpha,\beta\) be the roots of \(D(t)\) in an algebraic closure of \(\mathbb{F}_p\). Then

\[
\alpha+\beta=-\frac32,\qquad \alpha\beta=1,\qquad \alpha-\beta=\sqrt{-7}.
\]

The constant term of

\[
\frac{2t^{p+1}+3t+2t^{1-p}}{D(t)}
\]

can be found by expanding at infinity. The terms \(3t/D(t)\) and \(2t^{1-p}/D(t)\) have only negative powers of \(t\), so they contribute no constant term. Therefore

\[
B=[t^0]\frac{2t^{p+1}}{D(t)}.
\]

Using

\[
D(t)=2(t-\alpha)(t-\beta),
\]

we get

\[
\frac{2t^{p+1}}{D(t)}
=
\frac{t^{p+1}}{\alpha-\beta}
\left(\frac1{t-\alpha}-\frac1{t-\beta}\right).
\]

Expanding at infinity, the constant term is

\[
\frac{\alpha^p-\beta^p}{\alpha-\beta}.
\]

Hence

\[
B=\frac{\alpha^p-\beta^p}{\alpha-\beta}.
\]

If \(-7\) is a quadratic residue mod \(p\), then \(\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{F}_p\), so \(\alpha^p=\alpha\), \(\beta^p=\beta\), and \(B=1\).  
If \(-7\) is a quadratic nonresidue mod \(p\), then Frobenius swaps the roots: \(\alpha^p=\beta\), \(\beta^p=\alpha\), and \(B=-1\).

Thus, for \(p\neq 7\),

\[
B=\left(\frac{-7}{p}\right).
\]

For \(p=2027\),

\[
\left(\frac{-7}{2027}\right)
=
\left(\frac{-1}{2027}\right)
\left(\frac{7}{2027}\right).
\]

Since \(2027\equiv 3\pmod 4\),

\[
\left(\frac{-1}{2027}\right)=-1.
\]

By quadratic reciprocity,

\[
\left(\frac{7}{2027}\right)
=
-\left(\frac{2027}{7}\right).
\]

Now \(2027\equiv 4\pmod 7\), and \(4\) is a square modulo \(7\), so

\[
\left(\frac{2027}{7}\right)=1.
\]

Therefore

\[
\left(\frac{7}{2027}\right)=-1,
\qquad
\left(\frac{-7}{2027}\right)=1.
\]

So

\[
B=1.
\]

---

### 3. Finish

From (1),

\[
7S\equiv -4\pmod{2027}.
\]

Since

\[
7^{-1}\equiv 1448\pmod{2027},
\]

we get

\[
S\equiv -4\cdot 1448\equiv -5792\equiv 289\pmod{2027}.
\]

Therefore the remainder is

\[
\boxed{289}
\]
